root_cause.text: In fs/smb/client/smb2inode.c:smb2_unlink(), the SMB compound request iov arrays (`open_iov` and `close_iov`) were assigned into `rqst` without prior zero-initialization, so when `SMB2_open_init()` or `SMB2_close_init()` failed, later cleanup or `smb2_set_related()` operated on uninitialized iovec state and triggered an oops.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly says “If SMB2_open_init() or SMB2_close_init() fails … the iovs set @rqst will be left uninitialised, hence calling SMB2_open_free(), SMB2_close_free() or smb2_set_related() on them will oops,” and the patch adds `memset(open_iov, 0, sizeof(open_iov));`, `memset(&close_iov, 0, sizeof(close_iov));`, and moves `smb2_set_related(&rqst[1]);` to only run after `SMB2_close_init()` succeeds.

intent_record.what: A new initialization call was added to zero the open_iov array with memset(open_iov, 0, sizeof(open_iov)) before assigning it to rqst[0].rq_iov and setting rqst[0].rq_nvec.
intent_record.how: This ensures the request I/O vector array starts from a known zeroed state, preventing leftover stack data or uninitialized fields from being used when building the SMB2 unlink request, which can avoid incorrect request contents or unpredictable behavior at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize the close request iovec and only mark it related after successful SMB2_close_init to avoid using uninitialized SMB2 compound request state.
intent_record.what: The change adds a memset to zero-initialize close_iov before assigning it to rqst[1].rq_iov, and moves the smb2_set_related(&rqst[1]) call to occur only after SMB2_close_init succeeds instead of before checking rc.
intent_record.how: Zero-initializing close_iov prevents rqst[1] from using uninitialized iovec contents, and delaying smb2_set_related until after successful SMB2_close_init avoids marking an uninitialized or failed request as related, reducing the chance of malformed compound SMB2 close requests or misuse of partially initialized state.

candidates.rationale: This assigns the open_iov array into the request before any zero-initialization. If SMB2_open_init() fails later, cleanup or related compound handling can observe uninitialized iovec contents through rqst[0].
This assigns the close_iov storage into the request without prior initialization, exposing uninitialized iovec state if SMB2_close_init() fails and later code touches rqst[1].
This marks the close request as related even before checking whether SMB2_close_init() succeeded, causing later processing to operate on potentially uninitialized close_iov-backed request state.

vuln_statements.explanation: This stores the open_iov array into the SMB request before that iovec storage has been zero-initialized. If SMB2_open_init() later fails, cleanup or compound-request handling can dereference rqst[0] and observe uninitialized iovec state, matching the root cause.

This assigns close_iov into the second request without prior zero-initialization. When SMB2_close_init() fails, later cleanup or related-request processing can operate on rqst[1] backed by uninitialized iovec contents, contributing directly to the crash condition.

This marks the close request as a related compound request before verifying that SMB2_close_init() succeeded. As a result, later processing can treat rqst[1] as valid and operate on potentially uninitialized close_iov-backed request state, triggering the oops described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it directly shows the new compound request setup, initialization, failure paths, and cleanup. The vulnerable construct is present: `struct kvec open_iov[SMB2_CREATE_IOV_SIZE];` and `struct kvec close_iov;` are declared without explicit initialization, then assigned into request structures via `rqst[0].rq_iov = open_iov;` and `rqst[1].rq_iov = &close_iov;`. Although `memset(rqst, 0, sizeof(rqst));` clears the `rqst` array itself, it does not zero the storage backing `open_iov` or `close_iov`. The root-cause condition occurs because error handling can run after partial initialization failure: after `rc = SMB2_open_init(...); if (rc) goto err_free;` and `rc = SMB2_close_init(...); smb2_set_related(&rqst[1]); if (rc) goto err_free;`, the `err_free:` path unconditionally calls `SMB2_open_free(&rqst[0]);` and `SMB2_close_free(&rqst[1]);`. If either init function failed before fully initializing the associated iovecs, these free helpers may operate on uninitialized iovec state. Also, `smb2_set_related(&rqst[1]);` is invoked before checking `rc` from `SMB2_close_init()`, so it may also touch request state tied to an uninitialized `close_iov`. The fix described in the root cause would require prior zero-initialization of `open_iov` and `close_iov`, but this code does not do that. Therefore the bug is present and the fix is not.
